macro.title: What It Means — VWRA, Bonds, Gold & BTC

stories.headline: Twelve Gold Helmets, One Castle, Twenty-Eight Watches
stories.dek: Roger Dubuis has made the watch you wear to read a battlefield. On the dial of the Excalibur Kabuto Legacy, twelve hand-engraved 18-karat helmets — each a famed early-Edo commander — ring a miniature Edo Castle. It is 45mm of pink gold, limited to twenty-eight pieces, and priced, reportedly, at US$384,000. Wearable sculpture, aimed squarely at a reader who loves Japan.

stories.headline: The Biggest Preview Night Ever — and the Lowest of the Five
stories.dek: Spider-Man: Brand New Day took US$72 million in Thursday previews, the largest in Hollywood history, and a US$167-million-plus opening Friday, another record. Audiences gave it a 98 per cent that ties the MCU's best. And the critics, uniquely among Tom Holland's five, ranked it last. Both things are true, and the gap between them is the whole picture.

stories.headline: Japan Gets Dearer to Leave — and Changi Digs Its Future
stories.dek: The month's real developments for a Singapore flyer are small in dollars and large in signal: Japan's departure tax has tripled, the entry-fee creep continues across the region, SIA has settled its A380 map — and, under the ground at Changi, the tunnels to Terminal 5 are finished. Delta only; a route already covered gets a line, not a re-explainer.

stories.headline: A War That Has Run Out of Ceasefire
stories.dek: A five-night pause meant to give talks room ended the way the others did — with a "heavy wave" of American strikes and Iranian missiles answering. Then a drone crossed a line no one had crossed before, into Egypt, and set a gas terminal alight. Cairo can no longer pretend the war is someone else's.

stories.headline: The Bill and the Government Take the Same Word
stories.dek: Last week's story was a rename and a tariff arriving together; this weekend it settles into what it means for a household. The 17 per cent power rise is now on the bill, the ministry becomes "Energy, Trade and Industry" in October — and the island goes into a long National Day weekend with the cost of keeping the lights on quietly reframed as a matter of state.

stories.headline: The Buyer's Market Arrives — and the State Keeps Pouring
stories.dek: The froth is off. HDB resale prices fell a second straight quarter, a big mass-market launch cleared barely half its units, and low-balling is back on the forums. Into exactly that market the government has just launched a 1,200-home white site — and offered to build the roads itself. For an owner, the question shifts from "how high" to "how patient."

stories.headline: The Smuggling Probe Reaches a Desk in Taipei
stories.dek: For a year the export-control story was about which chips America would allow China to buy. This week it became about enforcement: Taiwan detained a man local media identify as an Nvidia employee in a widening probe into servers routed to China, and Jensen Huang went to Washington. The sovereignty fight has left the policy papers and reached a police station.

stories.headline: A Camera You Wear, So You Don't Have To Watch
stories.dek: The Looki L1 is a 32-gram clip-on that films your day and hands back a searchable, auto-edited diary of it — US$199, IP67, most of a day's battery. It is precisely the object a tech-forward reader is curious about and wary of: the logical end of the wearable, and a small ethics problem you strap to your shirt.

stories.headline: The Release That Deletes the Port Number — and the Net Behind It
stories.dek: Home Assistant 2026.8 lands this week, and the headline — no more typing ":8123" — is the least of it. Buried in the notes is the change a Lutron migrator actually wants: you can now set the network config from the interface, and the system applies it, then waits for you to confirm it still works before it commits. It is the end of locking yourself out with a bad edit.

stories.headline: Nine in Ten Parents Want the Phone Kept Close
stories.dek: The delta on last week's age-gating law is the parent's own contradiction. As school phone bans spread across more than thirty-five US states, a survey finds ninety per cent of parents still want their child reachable by phone at school — and parents at ban schools report more anxiety, not less. The panic is real. The evidence that bans fix it is thinner than the panic.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Portfolio Lens
stories.headline: Both Central Banks Blinked Hawkish — and the Sing Dollar Did the Reader's Work
stories.dek: The Fed held, but three members wanted a hike. The Bank of Japan held, but bought yen the same morning. And MAS quietly tightened a week earlier. For a VWRA-and-global-bonds holder banking in Singapore dollars, the week's mercy is currency: the same forces lifting his import bill are lifting the dollar he earns in. Market explanation, not advice.

stories.headline: Half a Kilo of Gold, and an Emperor's Ring on the Seabed
stories.dek: Off the Croatian island of Mljet, divers on a Byzantine wreck have raised the largest haul of Byzantine gold ever recovered from any Mediterranean shipwreck — more than six hundred grams, four ceremonial belt sets set with emeralds and rubies, and a signet ring bearing an emperor's image. Somebody important went down with that ship about thirteen hundred years ago. Probably.

stories.headline: The Friendship Recession Reaches Midlife
stories.dek: The quieter human story this weekend is not dating but its foundation. The share of adults with no close friend has climbed, the collapse is steepest among men — and for the first time a major survey finds men over forty-five lonelier than women. The cause is not too little contact. It is too much of the wrong kind, and a friendship that no longer forms by accident.

stories.headline: The Longevity Number You Can Buy for Twenty Dollars
stories.dek: The metric the longevity crowd re-centred on this summer is grip strength, and the reason is a study of five thousand older women: every seven kilograms of grip tracked twelve per cent lower mortality, the top quartile a third lower than the bottom. Grip is to total-body muscle what VO2 max is to the aerobic engine — and a hand dynamometer turns it into a home number. General information, not medical advice.

stories.headline: The On-Sale to Set an Alarm For
stories.dek: The autumn calendar is filling: The Weeknd and the first-ever Singapore Sprint weekend both land in early October, sumo tickets open on 8 August, and the long National Day weekend is here. Set the alarms — the good seats do not wait, and the sold-out ones breed scams.

stories.headline: The Five-Hundred-Metre Life
stories.dek: A generation in China is shrinking its world to the radius of a walk — the park downstairs, the wet market, a one-night stay one metro stop away — and calling it recovery. Chinese media has a name for it: huixue-gan xiaofei, "blood-replenishing consumption." Read from the ground, it is the sound of an experience economy downsizing to fit a flattened set of expectations — and the West has not written it up yet.
